column4: You are a beastling, a skinchanger. The ancient and feared gift of warging is yours to command. You can possess animals, entering their minds and controlling their bodies as if they were your own. This bond initially manifests in dreams, connecting you to a single creature with whom you share a special bond, but with practice, it expands to conscious control and a growing number of animals. A purchase of this allows you a free purchase of Furry(or Not So Furry) Friend.

At least in Westeros, magic is commonly believed to be dead or faded. This makes it harder for an aspiring mage to gain the patronage often necessary to get reagents and artefacts with which to do magic. Thankfully, you don’t have that problem! You are an expert in getting people to believe in your prowess, and can get them to sacrifice things on your behalf to power your magic. Yes, you too can convince a man to burn his own daughter!

A magnificent ship rivaling the legendary Sun Chaser in speed, durability, and design. Crafted with rare materials and imbued with subtle enchantments, this vessel can weather the fiercest storms, outrun pirates, and cross vast oceans with ease. It comes with a fully trained and loyal crew, ready to follow your every command. After this jump, the ship will adapt to fit the setting, remaining the best possible vessel for its time and place, whether that’s a spaceship, airship, or something else entirely.

This unassuming saddle, crafted from supple leather and silver-chased buckles, transforms any mount into a paragon of its kind. Place it on a donkey, and the beast becomes a warhorse with the speed of a Dornish sand steed and the endurance of a mammoth. Strap it to a lizard-lion, and the creature gains the cunning of a direwolf and the resilience of scaled plate. The saddle’s magic seeps into the mount, sharpening its instincts, tripling its stamina, and bending its loyalty unshakably to you.

The mount instinctively understands complex mental commands, leap chasms, feign death, or navigate tight city streets, and heals from near-fatal wounds overnight.

One of the most difficult aspects of warging is the helplessness that comes with leaving your own body behind. Not for you. With this upgrade, you can move, act, and even fight as your human self while your mind resides in another creature. It’s as though you inhabit two bodies at once, maintaining total awareness and coordination between them.

You have a subtle yet powerful gift: the ability to alter your appearance and that of items you touch. These changes are minor and cannot radically transform your body or disguise you entirely, but they are perfect for creating plausible deceptions. A slight shift in your features, the color of your eyes, or the cut of your clothing—these illusions are as real as the world believes them to be.

The dark art of the Faceless Men is yours to command. By harvesting the face of a willing subject—or removing it from the dead before decay claims it—you can take on their visage. Each face must be expertly preserved, a skill you instinctively possess. The magic imbued in these faces allows you to completely adopt the identity of their previous owner, from voice to mannerisms.

The alchemical arts are at your command. You possess the skills of a veteran member of the Alchemist's Guild of King's Landing, with a deep understanding of herbs, mixtures, and their medicinal uses. You are, of course, adept at creating wildfire, the volatile and destructive substance feared throughout Westeros.

You have unlocked the ability to transmute metals. With the right resources and focus, you can transform lead into gold or iron into steel. This power is not instantaneous and requires precise alchemical processes, but the results are undeniable. Beyond wealth, this skill has practical applications, such as forging superior tools or armaments from otherwise inferior materials.

You can command the primal forces of nature, bending them to your will. With the base purchase, you gain the ability to manipulate one of three elements—Air, Fire, or Water. While initially limited to minor feats and parlor tricks—stirring a breeze, sparking a flame, or rippling water—you have the foundation for growth into a powerful elemental adept. This perk may be purchased multiple times, once for each element, but upgrades apply only to the element selected for their respective purchase.

Does an area seem too cold to be natural? Is an area still volcanically deadly even almost five hundred years after the area was blighted by an unspecified doom? Perhaps being too long in an area will cause grayscale to latch onto you. Well, no longer. You are resistant to the effects of magical environments, be the source of a curse, damnation of fourteen gods, or just a shroud worn by the White Walkers. Now, it takes a bit longer for the effect to affect you. As long as you’re moving through the area, the magic won’t take hold on you, but the moment you stop with the intent of staying, the magic will very slowly start to work, 1% per ten minutes until you start leaving the area again. When it gets to 100%, the magic works on you as it would any other person.

Ordinarily, the overall strength of magic on Planetos is related to the tides of the earth, and the existence of magical creatures such as dragons. This means that in times of great magical power, the least of magicians could cast complex and powerful magics limited only to the strongest in times when magic wanes. Of course the flipside of this is that in times when magic isn’t strong, magicians can barely cast, with that same magician from before barely being able to summon sparks of fire with an ignition source. You gracefully avoid this problem, as magic seems to favour you preventing any such environmental factors affecting your power negatively.

column2: Crate of Weirwood, or Black-Barked Saplings
column4: Ten of either or five of both. They grow to full maturity within a year. Every ten years, another crate of twenty arrives. Weirwoods are sacred trees grown by the Children of the Forest and used as places of worship for those who follow the Old Gods. They have white bark, red sap and red leaves. The children often carve elaborate faces into the trunks as well, which the sap will swell up from, giving the appearance of tears. Black-Barked trees on the other hand are the trees Qarthian Warlocks use the leaves of, to make the Shade of Evening. Black-Barked trees have black bark and inky blue leaves. Both may have magical properties yet undiscovered, but will most likely relate to the two’s mystical properties. May be purchased multiple times. Both types of tree will create a mystical connection to trees of their fellow species, and can be used as a network to divine anything that has happened in their presence in the past or present. They can even be used to communicate through, over vast distances, as long as you have skills in divination.

The Asshai’i are a mysterious people, steeped in lore, versed in magic and myth. And few more than you. You have a natural gift for learning magic, for digging lore and artifacts out of the darkness of the past. You know the right way to step in haunted ruins, methods to translate and understand long-dead scripts, ways of testing for and diffusing lingering magic on that which you seek to take... while this does very little for your actual power or talent with magic, it does make you incredibly able when it comes to acquiring knowledge or artifacts. And knowledge is a power all its own.

A map enchanted much like the Marauder's Map, revealing the location of everyone within the Red Keep. It includes every room and hidden passage within the castle, though it is limited to a bird’s eye view.

This dark, beautifully crafted quill binds any contract signed with it to the full force of fate itself. Once someone signs their name, they are bound to their oath without question, though they remain unquestioning of the quill’s true nature. Anyone who uses the quill will be aware of the consequences of signing with it. Neither oaths nor terms can be violated by the signer without dire consequence.

You gain a weapon of your choice; it can be a sword, bow, spear, axe, dagger, or something more unique. You may select Valyrian steel or metal of a fallen star as the material, imbuing it with the power and prestige of legendary arms like the greatsword Dawn of House Dayne.

If you choose a bow, it may be crafted from materials like Dragonbone or the fabled Goldenheart wood of the Summer Islands. You’ll also receive a replenishing quiver of Valyrian steel or starmetal arrows, which vanish once they’ve served their purpose and are out of sight, ensuring they can’t be used by anyone but you.

This weapon may take on whatever appearance you desire, and regardless of its form, this weapon will function impeccably, even if it might otherwise seem impractical.

Where most wargs can control only one creature at a time, you wield dominion over entire packs. Like Varamyr Sixskins, you can command multiple animals simultaneously, coordinating them as extensions of your will. Whether it’s a swarm of ravens, a pack of wolves, or a pride of lions, your influence over beasts knows few limits.

There was a divinity in your family history, and no matter how many generations the benefits have skipped over, they are shining through you now. You’re a little taller, a lot smarter, a little more attractive and charming, and a fair bit stronger and faster than you were before. You will live maybe half again as long as others of your kind, and be in full vigour until the end of your years. This works as a capstone booster, boosting all of your perks slightly, but most especially all of your capstone perks. The enhanced version of the perks are in the notes, as are the height differences.

Those who sing the songs of the earth have many gifts. Chief amongst these is the ability to speak the True Tongue, a great affinity for magic, and a deep spiritual connection to nature which increases potency of nature based magics. The True Tongue is based on the sounds of the world, including things like wind on leaves, rain on water and the sound of stones in a brook. By binding themselves to a weirwood, an earthsinger may live for far longer than any other of their kind. There is evidence that some of the Children currently alive today were amongst those who created the Others 12,000 years ago.

More than any other beings, the White Walkers are the children of winter. This manifests in their immensely powerful winter magic, as well as their ability to reshape ice into any form they wish. At first, all you will be able to do is create crude forms out of ice, and affect the weather around you towards the cooler side. But as you gain experience, you will learn to create weapons of ice capable of cutting castle forged steel like butter as well as alter the weather on a large enough scale to plunge an entire continent into a decades long ice age. As one of the others, you also possess the ability to raise vast armies of the dead as wights. Other species can do this if they practice, however White Walkers have a greater affinity, and are capable of simultaneously raising hosts numbering in the thousands with a bit of effort.

column3: A Song of Ice and Fire Jumpchain
column4: You can use your blood to set alight your weapon. Such fire blazes incredibly hot and is unnaturally intimidating to your enemies and heartening to your allies but will ruin ordinary steel.

The First Men would name you a greenseer; the Targaryens would call you a dreamer. You possess the rare and enigmatic gift of prophecy. This ability grants you premonitions, glimpses of the future that come in visions, dreams, or sudden flashes of insight. These visions can be cryptic and open to interpretation, with truths often hidden beneath layers of symbolism.  While the Sight can be a powerful tool, beware: prophecy is a double-edged sword. Misinterpretation of what you see can lead to unintended consequences, and knowing the future does not always mean you can change it.

Like Garth Greenhand before you, you are a fountain of life and vitality, a living embodiment of fertility and abundance. Women touched by your blessing are granted extraordinary fertility, often bearing twins or triplets, while crops thrive and flourish in your presence. Wherever you tread, the land awakens: barren fields ripen with grain, orchards yield fruit beyond expectation, and flowers bloom in your wake. This gift of life flows from you effortlessly, rejuvenating both people and nature alike. Your presence is a blessing to any who rely on the land, ensuring prosperity wherever you choose to wander.

A simple yet ominous iron coin bearing the mark of the Faceless Men. When you present this coin and whisper the name of your intended target, a Faceless Man will ensure their death within a week—no matter where they hide or how well-guarded they are. This can only be used once per year, and the Faceless Men will not divulge how they completed the task.

The magic of life and death, necromancy is a fell magic used by many,including Qyburn, the Others, some Qarthian Warlocks, and the Bloodstone Emperor. By purchasing this perk, you have gained the ability to raise groups of undead wights bound by your will and life force, as well as the ability to perform a true resurrection once per year.

The Rhoyne’s children did not kneel to dragons. They fought with currents, not swords, and drowned fire in the Mother’s embrace. Now, her power flows through you. You wield the ancient water magic of the Rhoynar, a legacy of the river priests who once defied Valyria itself. While crude hydrokinesis is a small portion of this gift, the Mother’s blessings run deeper. You can summon impenetrable fogs that stretch for miles, shrouding fleets or armies in mist that only you and your allies can see through. Wounds immersed in flowing water knit together under your touch, bones mending and gashes closing as if time itself bends to the river’s song. Poisoned wine turns harmless at your command, and blighted wells run clear again. Yet the Rhoyne’s mercy is matched by her wrath, her currents answer your fury, dragging ships beneath the waves or crashing torrents against castle walls.

Your mastery extends beyond ordinary smithing to include secret techniques and alchemical processes that elevate your creations into legendary artefacts. You can forge entirely new Valyrian Steel without needing dragonfire, making you perhaps the only living individual capable of creating these legendary blades from scratch. Though the process is still resource-intensive and arduous, the results are unparalleled.

You have inherited the ingenuity and creativity that Bran the Builder was said to possess, granting you the ability to design and construct monumental projects that rival the greatest wonders of Westeros. Fortresses that defy siegecraft, walls that stand against the ages, and sprawling structures that awe all who see them are within your grasp.  You can complete immense projects in a fraction of the time and with far fewer resources than should be possible, your efficiency supernatural. The things you create are not only practical and enduring but works of art in their own right, imbued with a sense of purpose and majesty that captures the imagination. Whether constructing a castle, designing defenses, or raising a tower to scrape the heavens, your work is guaranteed to stand for generations as a marvel of the world.

column3: A Song of Ice and Fire Jumpchain
column4: Once a week you may produce a shadow. Such a shadow will obey your command to assassinate someone. Highly effective but must have surfaces to walk on. Ineffective against magical targets.
